theorem_title: No bounded-time descent rank from a finite monotone palette
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$. Let $r,B\in\mathbb N$, let $f_0,\ldots,f_{r-1}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be nondecreasing on inputs at least $B$, and let $\sigma:\mathbb N\to\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$. Let $V:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $V(n)=f_{\sigma(n)}(n)$ for $n\ge B$.

For any further natural threshold $B'$ and time bound $H$, the following uniform rank-descent assertion is false:

$$
\neg\bigl(\forall n\ge B',\ \exists j,\ 1\le j\le H\ \land\ V(T^j(n))<V(n)\bigr).
$$

The obstruction concerns this finite-palette, uniformly bounded-time proof architecture. It does not imply nontermination of any Collatz orbit.
